components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.

example.pinyin: Hāhā, zhēn hǎoxiào!
example.english: Haha, that's so funny!
example.fact: 哈 is an onomatopoeic character for laughter, written as 哈哈 for 'haha'. It also appears in 哈欠 (yawn), and in transliterations of names like 哈佛 (Harvard).

examples.hanzi: 哈哈，这个笑话真有意思！
examples.pinyin: Hāhā, zhège xiàohua zhēn yǒu yìsi!
examples.english: Haha, this joke is really funny!

examples.pinyin: Hā, nǐ zhōngyú lái le!
examples.english: Ha, you finally came!

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks: 酒, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 醒 is sobering up, then waking.
星 (xīng) sounds exactly like 醒 (tone differs).

example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang liù diǎn xǐng le.
example.english: I woke up at six in the morning.
example.fact: 醒 is often used as a result complement: 睡醒 (wake up from sleep) and 叫醒 (wake someone up). It also means to sober up (酒醒) and to become aware (觉醒, 提醒 'to remind').

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou xǐng de?
examples.english: When did you wake up?

examples.hanzi: 他喝了很多，现在还没醒酒。
examples.pinyin: Tā hēle hěn duō, xiànzài hái méi xǐngjiǔ.
examples.english: He drank a lot and still hasn't sobered up.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen fēn yi fēn ba.
example.english: Let's split it.
example.fact: 分 is highly versatile: a minute (五分钟), a point in a score (三分), a cent (一分钱) and the verb 'to divide'. In 分数 (score) and 十分 (very), the reading and use differ.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn shí fēn.
examples.english: It's ten past three now.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试他得了九十分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì tā déle jiǔshí fēn.
examples.english: He scored ninety on this exam.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 他终于完成了这项任务。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú wánchéng le zhè xiàng rènwu.
example.english: He finally completed this task.
example.fact: 完 by itself is one of Mandarin's most common resultative verb complements, tacked onto other verbs to mean "finish doing X" (吃完 "finish eating," 做完 "finish doing") — 完成 is the separate, full verb for "to complete" a formal task or project, and the two are not interchangeable despite sharing a character.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wánchéng zuòyè le ma?
examples.english: Have you finished your homework?

examples.hanzi: 这个工作我们明天能完成。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngzuò wǒmen míngtiān néng wánchéng.
examples.english: We can complete this job tomorrow.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: This movie is great.
example.fact: 部 is a measure word for films, books and works (一部电影), and a noun for departments and ministries (外交部, 部门). It also means 'a part', in 部分 (part) and 全部 (all).

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù shǒujī hěn hǎoyòng.
examples.english: This phone is very handy.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài xiāoshòubù gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works in the sales department.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: 昨 is a past day.
乍 (zhà) is a close sound clue for zuó; 乍 also in 作 zuò, 怎 zěn and 炸 zhà.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.

example.hanzi: 昨晚我做了一个奇怪的梦。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn wǒ zuò le yí gè qíguài de mèng.
example.english: Last night I had a strange dream.
example.fact: 昨晚 follows a simple, productive template — [day-word] + 晚 ("evening") — shared by 今晚 ("tonight") and 明晚 ("tomorrow night") — so once 昨/今/明 (yesterday/today/tomorrow) are known, all three time words come for free.

examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn nǐ shuì de hǎo ma?
examples.english: Did you sleep well last night?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn shíyī diǎn cái huíjiā.
examples.english: I didn't get home until eleven last night.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì tóngxué.
example.english: We are classmates.
example.fact: 同 appears in 同学 (classmate), 同事 (coworker), 同意 (agree), 不同 (different), 一同 (together). It also acts as a preposition 'with', as in 同…一起.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài tóng yí ge bān.
examples.english: We are in the same class.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóngyì nǐ de kànfǎ.
examples.english: I agree with your view.

components.note: 医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 我奶奶昨天住进了医院。
example.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai zuótiān zhù jìn le yīyuàn.
example.english: My grandmother was admitted to the hospital yesterday.
example.fact: 院 (literally "courtyard") is a common suffix for buildings organized as an institution — the same 院 appears in 学院 ("college"), 电影院 ("cinema"), and 法院 ("court") — so recognizing the "courtyard/institution" suffix helps guess the meaning of many other buildings.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào qù yīyuàn kànbìng.
examples.english: I'm going to the hospital to see a doctor tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn lí zhèlǐ bú tài yuǎn.
examples.english: The hospital isn't too far from here.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 这个办法不行,我们再想想。
example.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ bùxíng, wǒmen zài xiǎngxiang.
example.english: This method won't work, let's think again.
example.fact: Beyond a plain refusal ("no good, won't do"), 不行 doubles as a common colloquial intensifier attached after 得 to mean "extremely" (累得不行, "exhausted beyond belief") — a dramatic stand-in for "extremely" in that same grammatical slot.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò bù xíng.
examples.english: Doing it this way won't work.

examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu qián kě bù xíng.
examples.english: It won't work without money.

components.note: 而 (and, but) — oldest form is a beard (compare 须 xū, beard), later borrowed for the conjunction; 而 survives in 耐 nài.
己 (self) — 已 looks like 己 with the gap closed, so do not mix them up. Memory aid: the opening is closed — it is already done (已经).

example.hanzi: 我只是跟你开玩笑而已。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì gēn nǐ kāi wánxiào éryǐ.
example.english: I was just joking with you, that's all.
example.fact: 而已 always sits at the very end of a sentence and almost always partners with 只(是) earlier in the clause ("只是...而已", "it's just...that's all") — a fixed sentence-final particle rather than a word that can move around, underlining "nothing more to it."

examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐshì ge háizi éryǐ.
examples.english: He's just a child, that's all.

examples.hanzi: 我不过说说而已,别当真。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ búguò shuōshuo éryǐ, bié dàngzhēn.
examples.english: I was just saying it, don't take it seriously.

components.note: 半 (half) — 牛 (an ox) divided in two by 八: half. Seen in 一半 half, 半夜 midnight.

example.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn bàn.
example.english: It is half past three now.
example.fact: 半 comes after the number and measure word: 三点半 (3:30), 一个半小时 (one and a half hours). In 半夜 and 半路 it means 'in the middle of'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ děngle bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I waited for half an hour.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ bàn bēi rèshuǐ.
examples.english: Please give me half a cup of hot water.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàngmiàn fàngzhe yì běn shū.
example.english: There's a book placed on top of the table.
example.fact: Beyond its literal spatial sense, 上面 extends abstractly to mean "the above-mentioned" when referring back to something already said in a text (上面提到的问题, "the problem mentioned above") — the same up/down metaphor that structures how many languages talk about textual sequence.

examples.pinyin: Shū zài zhuōzi shàngmiàn.
examples.english: The book is on the table.

examples.pinyin: Shàngmiàn xiězhe shénme?
examples.english: What does it say on top?

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Nà zuò fángzi háishi lǎo yàngzi.
example.english: That house still looks the same as before.
example.fact: 子 in 样子 is the same light grammatical suffix seen in 孩子 (in the companion character-deck's pilot batch) — worn down from its original meaning "child" into a semantically empty ending that simply signals "this is a noun," attached here to 样 ("kind, appearance").

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de yàngzi hěn qíguài.
examples.english: He looks strange today.

examples.pinyin: Zhège yàngzi hǎokàn ma?
examples.english: Does this style look good?

components.note: 小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.

example.pinyin: Tā chī de hěn shǎo.
example.english: He eats very little.
example.fact: 少 has two readings: shǎo ('few', as here) and shào ('young', as in 少年). Its opposite is 多 (duō, many), and 少 + verb pattern: 少吃点 means 'eat a bit less'.

examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè de yǔ bǐjiào shǎo.
examples.english: There's relatively little rain this month.

examples.hanzi: 少喝一点儿酒对身体好。
examples.pinyin: Shǎo hē yìdiǎnr jiǔ duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Drinking less alcohol is good for your health.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 起, 越, 赶: going toward something that attracts you.
取 (qǔ) is a close sound clue for qù; 取 also in 娶 qǔ and 聚 jù.

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de gùshi hěn yǒuqù.
example.english: The story in this book is very interesting.
example.fact: 有趣 follows a common Chinese pattern where 有 ("to have") plus an abstract noun forms an adjective — literally "has interest, has fun" — the same template behind 有名 ("famous," literally "has a name") and 有用 ("useful," literally "has use").

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: This movie is very interesting.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge yǒuqù de rén.
examples.english: He's an interesting person.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.

example.pinyin: Qǐng tí yíxià zhège wèntí.
example.english: Please bring up this question.
example.fact: 提 literally means to carry something by hand (提包), and extends to 'to raise' in 提高 (improve), 提出 (put forward) and 提醒 (remind). It's also the character in 提前 (in advance).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tí yí ge wèntí.
examples.english: I'd like to raise a question.

examples.hanzi: 他提着一个很重的箱子。
examples.pinyin: Tā tízhe yí ge hěn zhòng de xiāngzi.
examples.english: He is carrying a very heavy suitcase.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.

example.pinyin: “Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le.” “Méiguānxi.”
example.english: "Sorry, I'm late." "It's okay, no worries."
example.fact: 没关系 literally means "[it] doesn't have a connection, a relationship" (没 + 关系) — much like English "no worries" or "it's nothing," it downplays a problem by denying that it has any real bearing on anything, rather than directly saying "it's fine."

examples.pinyin: Méi guānxi, xiàcì zài lái.
examples.english: It's okay, come again next time.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù lái yě méi guānxi.
examples.english: It doesn't matter if you don't come.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de Měiguó péngyou jiào Jiékè.
example.english: My American friend is called Jack.
example.fact: 杰克 is a phonetic transliteration of the English name "Jack," chosen primarily to approximate the sound — but as is common practice when transliterating foreign names, the characters were also picked for their agreeable meanings: 杰 ("outstanding, heroic") and 克 ("to overcome, be capable of").

examples.pinyin: Jiékè shì wǒ de tóngshì.
examples.english: Jack is my coworker.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Jiékè ma?
examples.english: Do you know Jack?

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.pinyin: “Wǒ míngtiān yào jiéhūn le.” “Zhēn de ma?”
example.english: "I'm getting married tomorrow." "Really?"
example.fact: Bare 真 already works as an intensifier before an adjective (真好, "really good"), but adding 的 to make 真的 is what lets the word stand entirely on its own as an exclamation or question ("真的?!", "Really?!") — the 的 here doesn't mark possession, it just closes off the phrase so it can function independently.

examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi shì zhēn de.
examples.english: This story is true.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dōngxi zhēn de hěn hǎoyòng.
examples.english: This thing is really useful.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 大部分学生都同意这个计划。
example.pinyin: Dà bùfen xuésheng dōu tóngyì zhège jìhuà.
example.english: The majority of students agree with this plan.
example.fact: 部分 rarely stands completely alone as a bare noun in speech — it's usually paired with a modifier like 大 (大部分, "most, the majority") or 一 (一部分, "a portion") rather than used by itself the way English "part" often is.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì shū de dì yī bùfen.
examples.english: This is the first part of the book.

examples.hanzi: 他把蛋糕分成了三部分。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ dàngāo fēnchéngle sān bùfen.
examples.english: He divided the cake into three parts.

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.

example.hanzi: 老师对学生的要求很严格。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng de yāoqiú hěn yángé.
example.english: The teacher's requirements for students are very strict.
example.fact: Like 工作 in the companion character-deck's pilot batch, 要求 works as both a verb ("to demand, request") and a noun ("a requirement, demand") with no change in form — Chinese frequently lets a single word cross that verb/noun line for free.

examples.hanzi: 老板要求我们准时上班。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn yāoqiú wǒmen zhǔnshí shàngbān.
examples.english: The boss requires us to be on time.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge xiǎo yāoqiú.
examples.english: I have a small request.

components.note: 米 (rice) — grain and food, as in 粉 powder, 糕 cake, 精 refined: 糟 is dregs of fermented rice, then spoiled.
曹 (cáo) is a close sound clue for zāo; 曹 also in 遭 zāo and 槽 cáo.
米 (rice) — grain and food, as in 粉 powder, 糟, 精: cakes were first made from rice flour.
羔 (gāo, lamb) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 糟糕,我把钥匙忘在家里了!
example.pinyin: Zāogāo, wǒ bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiā lǐ le!
example.english: Oh no, I forgot my keys at home!
example.fact: Unlike many two-character words that split their meaning evenly across both syllables, 糟糕's second syllable 糕 ("cake") contributes essentially nothing to the meaning "terrible" — it's there mainly for rhythm and rhyme with 糟 ("spoiled dregs," the syllable that actually carries the negative sense).

examples.pinyin: Zāogāo, wǒ wàngle dài shǒujī!
examples.english: Oh no, I forgot my phone!

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì zāogāo jí le.
examples.english: The weather today is terrible.

components.note: 阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.hanzi: 除了英语,他还会说法语。
example.pinyin: Chúle Yīngyǔ, tā hái huì shuō Fǎyǔ.
example.english: Besides English, he can also speak French.
example.fact: Like 所有...都... noted in the companion pilot batch, 除了 usually works as half of a two-part frame — 除了 X,(大家)都/也/还 Y — where the second clause's 都 (an exclusive "all" reading) or 也/还 (an additive "also" reading) determines whether 除了 ends up meaning "except" or "besides."

examples.pinyin: Chúle tā, dàjiā dōu lái le.
examples.english: Everyone came except him.

examples.hanzi: 除了工作,我还喜欢画画。
examples.pinyin: Chúle gōngzuò, wǒ hái xǐhuan huàhuà.
examples.english: Besides work, I also like painting.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.
易 (yì) is a loose sound clue for 踢 tī, 赐 cì and 惕 tì; the meaning "easy" comes from "change" and its early lizard picture is unproven.

example.pinyin: Zhège zì hěn róngyì xiěcuò.
example.english: This character is easy to write incorrectly.
example.fact: 容易 and its near-synonym 简单 (also in this batch, rank 336) overlap but aren't identical — 容易 describes how easy an action is to carry out or how likely an outcome is (容易错, "easy/likely to go wrong"), while 简单 describes something's inherent lack of complexity, closer to English "simple" than "easy."

examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tí hěn róngyì.
examples.english: This question is very easy.

examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān hěn róngyì gǎnmào.
examples.english: It's easy to catch a cold in winter.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎochí ānjìng.
example.english: Please keep quiet.
example.fact: 保 (from a caretaker cradling a child, per its component breakdown) contributes "to protect, look after," while 持 (built from the hand radical 扌) contributes "to hold" — together 保持 paints a literal image of protectively holding something steady, fitting its modern sense "to maintain, keep."

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎochí liánxì.
examples.english: We should keep in touch.

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān yùndòng, bǎochí jiànkāng.
examples.english: He exercises every day to stay healthy.

components.note: 虫 (insect, small creature) — family of 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake. In 虽 it is a leftover of 雖; 'although' has nothing to do with insects.
雖 (traditional) — 虫 plus 唯 (wéi) as sound. 虽 is a simplified shape for it, a grammar word whose parts do not carry its meaning.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 虽然外面很冷,但是我们还是决定出去跑步。
example.pinyin: Suīrán wàimiàn hěn lěng, dànshì wǒmen háishi juédìng chūqù pǎobù.
example.english: Although it's cold outside, we still decided to go running.
example.fact: 虽然 belongs to the same family of correlative conjunction pairs as 因为...所以... (flagged in the companion pilot batch) — it almost always shows up with 但是 or 可是 in the following clause, and dropping the second half tends to sound incomplete to a native ear even though English "although" alone is often enough.

examples.hanzi: 虽然很累,但是我很开心。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì wǒ hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: Although I'm tired, I'm very happy.

examples.hanzi: 他虽然年轻,却很有经验。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán niánqīng, què hěn yǒu jīngyàn.
examples.english: Although he's young, he's very experienced.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 助, 男, 努: handling things takes effort. The two dots stand in for 辡 of the traditional 辦.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ lái bàn.
example.english: I'll handle this matter.
example.fact: 办 is the practical verb for getting things done: 办事 (run errands), 办公室 (office) and 办法 (method), as in 没办法 ('no way'). It also means to set up or run, as in 办学校 or 办婚礼.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ zěnme bàn?
examples.english: How are you going to handle this?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù bàn yì zhāng yínhángkǎ.
examples.english: I need to get a bank card.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我没想到会在这里遇见你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ méi xiǎngdào huì zài zhèlǐ yùjiàn nǐ.
example.english: I didn't expect to run into you here.
example.fact: 想到 emphasizes an idea suddenly arriving in the mind — its negative form 没想到 ("didn't expect, would never have thought") is one of the most common exclamations in spoken Chinese — while its close cousin 想起 emphasizes recalling something already known, a distinction carried entirely by the verb complement (到 "arriving at" vs 起 "rising up") after 想.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎngdàole yí ge hǎo bànfǎ.
examples.english: I thought of a good way.

examples.hanzi: 你有没有想到过这个问题?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu xiǎngdàoguo zhège wèntí?
examples.english: Did you ever think of this problem?

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.

example.pinyin: Tā jiāo wǒmen shùxué.
example.english: He teaches us math.
example.fact: 教 has two readings: jiāo (the verb 'to teach', as here) and jiào (noun, as in 教育 'education' and 宗教 'religion'). The double-object pattern 教 + person + subject (教我中文) is typical.

examples.pinyin: Wáng lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen Yīngyǔ.
examples.english: Teacher Wang teaches us English.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jiāo wǒ zuòfàn ma?
examples.english: Can you teach me how to cook?

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wánquán lǐjiě nǐ de gǎnshòu.
example.english: I completely understand your feelings.
example.fact: 理解 leans more formal and analytical than the everyday verb 懂 ("to understand, get it") — 理解 suits comprehending a complex idea, argument, or someone's feelings, while 懂 is the blunt, all-purpose "get it" used constantly in casual speech (懂了吗?, "get it?").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǐjiě nǐ de xīnqíng.
examples.english: I understand how you feel.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jù huà hěn nán lǐjiě.
examples.english: This sentence is hard to understand.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.hanzi: 警察在现场找到了重要的证据。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài xiànchǎng zhǎodào le zhòngyào de zhèngjù.
example.english: The police found important evidence at the scene.
example.fact: 证据 combines 证 ("to prove, certify," literally "speaking the correct truth") with 据 ("to rely on, a basis," literally "grasped in hand") — literally "a proven basis to rely on," which is why it's the standard word reached for in legal and investigative contexts.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme zhèngjù ma?
examples.english: Do you have any evidence?

examples.hanzi: 没有证据,我不能相信他。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu zhèngjù, wǒ bù néng xiāngxìn tā.
examples.english: Without evidence, I can't believe him.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.

example.pinyin: Sān jiā wǔ děngyú bā.
example.english: Three plus five equals eight.
example.fact: 加 is the verb 'to add' and the plus sign, and it's also used in 加油 ('add oil', 'go for it!'), 加班 (work overtime) and 加入 (join). 加油 is also the word for filling up a car.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiā yìdiǎnr táng.
examples.english: Please add a little sugar.

examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ yào jiābān.
examples.english: I have to work overtime tonight.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脑 brain, 脚 foot); 脸 is a body part, the face.
佥 (qiān) — loose hint — 脸 is liǎn; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn, 险 xiǎn and 验 yàn, all ending in -ǎn.

example.pinyin: Tā de liǎn hóng le.
example.english: His face turned red.
example.fact: 脸 is the face as a body part and also 'face' in the social sense: 丢脸 (lose face), 不要脸 (shameless) and 给面子 are close cousins of this idea. It takes the measure word 张 (一张脸) and appears in 洗脸 (wash one's face) and 笑脸 (smiling face).

examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shang dàizhe xiàoróng.
examples.english: She has a smile on her face.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù xǐxi liǎn ba.
examples.english: Go wash your face.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo strips, once written on, as in 笔, 等, 管: a slip, so simple and brief.
间 (jiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 这个游戏的规则很简单。
example.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì de guīzé hěn jiǎndān.
example.english: The rules of this game are very simple.
example.fact: 简 originally named the bamboo strips ancient Chinese texts were written on (per its component breakdown) — one plausible account links 简's later sense of "simple, terse" to writing brief enough to fit on just a few such strips, though like many bamboo-radical etymologies this connection is more suggestive than certain.

examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: This question is very simple.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng jiǎndān de huà gàosu wǒ.
examples.english: Please tell me in simple words.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.pinyin: Měi gè rén de kànfǎ dōu bùtóng.
example.english: Everyone's views are different.
example.fact: 不同 and 不一样 (built by simply negating 一样, "same," from the companion pilot batch) both mean "different," but they tend to divide labor: 不同 reads more formal and comfortably modifies a noun directly (不同的意见, "differing opinions"), while 不一样 feels more colloquial and usually sits after the subject as a predicate (这两个不一样, "these two are different").

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de kànfǎ bù tóng.
examples.english: Our views are different.

examples.hanzi: 这两个城市有很大的不同。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge chéngshì yǒu hěn dà de bù tóng.
examples.english: These two cities are very different.

components.note: 大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 王夫人今天没有来开会。
example.pinyin: Wáng fūren jīntiān méiyǒu lái kāihuì.
example.english: Mrs. Wang didn't come to the meeting today.
example.fact: 夫人 mirrors 先生 (in the companion pilot batch) as a formal title attached after a surname — but it's normally used to address or refer to someone else's wife respectfully; calling one's own wife 夫人 in casual conversation sounds stiff or old-fashioned to modern ears.

examples.pinyin: Lǐ fūren shì yí wèi lǎoshī.
examples.english: Mrs. Li is a teacher.

examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, fūren yào hē diǎn shénme?
examples.english: Excuse me, what would madam like to drink?

components.note: 父 (father) — a hand holding a stone axe, an image of the household head who works and rules.
母 (mother) — a woman 女 with two dots for breasts: a nursing mother. 母 also appears in 每 měi, 海 hǎi and 梅 méi.

example.pinyin: Wǒ fùmǔ zhù zài xiāngxià.
example.english: My parents live in the countryside.
example.fact: 父 and 母 are old, classical single-syllable words for "father" and "mother," but in modern everyday speech they've mostly been displaced by the colloquial doubled forms 爸爸 and 妈妈 — 父 and 母 now survive mainly inside formal compounds like 父母, 父亲, 母亲, and 祖父母 ("grandparents").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào gěi fùmǔ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'm going to call my parents.

examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ dōu xīwàng háizi xìngfú.
examples.english: Parents all want their children to be happy.

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).

example.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi hěn zhòng.
example.english: This box is very heavy.
example.fact: 重 has two main readings: zhòng ('heavy, serious', as here and in 重要, 严重) and chóng ('again, to repeat', as in 重新, 重复). Tone and meaning change with the reading, so look at the context: 重来 (chónglái) means 'do over'.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo tài zhòng le.
examples.english: This bag is too heavy.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn zhòngyào, bié wàng le.
examples.english: This matter is important, don't forget.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 思; 恩 is kindness, gratitude of the heart.
因 (yīn) is only a loose sound hint for ēn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn jìde nǐ de ēnqíng.
example.english: I will always remember your kindness.
example.fact: 恩 is a formal, warm word for benevolence, seen in 恩人 (benefactor), 感恩 (be grateful) and 恩爱 (loving, said of couples). 感恩节 is the Chinese name for Thanksgiving.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn gǎnxiè nǐ de ēnqíng.
examples.english: I will always be grateful for your kindness.

examples.hanzi: 他们是一对恩爱的夫妻。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yí duì ēn'ài de fūqī.
examples.english: They are a loving married couple.

components.note: 曾 (céng) began as a picture of a steamer (甑 zèng adds 瓦); the past-time meaning is borrowed. 曾 also gives 增 zēng, 层 céng and 赠 zèng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ céngjīng qùguo nàlǐ.
example.english: I have been there before.
example.fact: 曾 is nearly always seen as 曾经 ('once, previously'), which is used with 过 to talk about past experiences, as in 我曾经去过北京. It is also a surname (read Zēng), which is the reading in names like 曾国藩.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ céngjīng zài Shànghǎi gōngzuòguo.
examples.english: I once worked in Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Tā céngjīng shì wǒ de tóngzhuō.
examples.english: He used to be my desk mate.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.pinyin: Shìshí zhèngmíng tā shì duì de.
example.english: Facts proved that he was right.
example.fact: 事实 narrows down 事 ("matter, affair" — the same root behind 事情 in the companion pilot batch) with 实 ("real, solid, true"), giving a word that specifically stresses factuality, where plain 事情 just means "a matter" without any claim about whether it's true.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge shìshí.
examples.english: This is a fact.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào miànduì shìshí.
examples.english: You have to face the facts.

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 我们的飞机明天早上起飞。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de fēijī míngtiān zǎoshang qǐfēi.
example.english: Our plane takes off tomorrow morning.
example.fact: 飞机 is a transparent modern coinage — literally "flying machine" — built from the same productive 机 ("machine") suffix found in 手机 ("cellphone," literally "hand machine") and 洗衣机 ("washing machine"), a go-to pattern whenever Chinese needed a word for a new mechanical invention.

examples.pinyin: Fēijī wǎndiǎn le yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: The plane was delayed by an hour.

examples.hanzi: 我第一次坐飞机去中国。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dì yī cì zuò fēijī qù Zhōngguó.
examples.english: It was my first time flying to China.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店, 床, 度: a hall or courtyard.
廷 (tíng) gives the exact sound; also in 挺 tǐng and 艇 tǐng.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè xìngfú de jiātíng.
example.english: This is a happy family.
example.fact: Plain 家 is the all-purpose, everyday word for "home" or "family" (我家, "my home/family"), while 家庭 reads more formal and abstract, treating the family as a social unit — the kind of word that shows up in phrases like 家庭教育 ("family education") rather than in casual talk about one's own household.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiātíng hěn xiǎo.
examples.english: My family is small.

examples.hanzi: 他来自一个普通的家庭。
examples.pinyin: Tā láizì yí ge pǔtōng de jiātíng.
examples.english: He comes from an ordinary family.

components.note: 象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì tóu xiàng.
example.english: There is an elephant in the zoo.
example.fact: 象 is 'elephant' on its own (usually 大象) and also 'appearance' in 印象 (impression), 现象 (phenomenon), 想象 (imagine) and 对象 (target, partner). 象 and 像 are often confused: 像 means 'like' or 'to resemble'.

examples.pinyin: Dàxiàng de bízi hěn cháng.
examples.english: An elephant's trunk is very long.

examples.hanzi: 她给我留下了很好的印象。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ liúxiàle hěn hǎo de yìnxiàng.
examples.english: She left me a very good impression.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.pinyin: Tā zài zhuāng shuì.
example.english: He is pretending to be asleep.
example.fact: 装 has many uses: 'to pack/load' (装箱子), 'to install' (安装), 'to pretend' (装傻, 装睡), and 'clothes' (服装, 西装). It's a good example of how one character can mix 'putting on' clothes and 'putting on' an act.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ dōngxi zhuāngjìn xiāngzi lǐ.
examples.english: Please pack the things into the box.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī zhuāngle xīn ruǎnjiàn.
examples.english: I installed new software on my phone.

components.note: 必 (bì) is a close sound clue for mì; 必 also gives 密 mì and 蜜 mì.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.hanzi: 这是我们两个人之间的秘密。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen liǎng gè rén zhī jiān de mìmì.
example.english: This is a secret between the two of us.
example.fact: 秘 and 密 both independently carry a "hidden, concealed" sense — 秘密 reinforces two already near-synonymous roots into one noun, the same word-building strategy seen elsewhere in this deck in words like 声音. As a side note, 秘 is also read bì in the surname 祕/秘, an uncommon reading unrelated to its ordinary "secret" sense.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gàosu nǐ yí ge mìmì.
examples.english: Let me tell you a secret.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào tì wǒ bǎoshǒu mìmì.
examples.english: You must keep my secret for me.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí gè hǎo bànfǎ.
example.english: I have a good solution.
example.fact: 法 is law (法律, 犯法) and also 'method' (办法, 方法, 想法). It is the character in 法国 (France) and 法语 (French), as 法 alone refers to France, derived from the old transliteration.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme hǎo bànfǎ ma?
examples.english: Do you have any good ideas?

examples.pinyin: Tā huì shuō Fǎyǔ hé Yīngyǔ.
examples.english: He can speak French and English.

components.note: 尸 (body) — originally a person seated or lying; as a radical it is in 尾 tail, 层 floor, 居 reside, 屋 house.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 警方在河边发现了一具尸体。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zài hébiān fāxiàn le yí jù shītǐ.
example.english: The police discovered a corpse by the riverside.
example.fact: 尸体 is the neutral, clinical word for "corpse," common in news and forensic contexts — Chinese also has the more respectful, softened 遗体 ("the remains") for contexts where dignity toward the deceased matters, a register split similar to English choosing between "corpse," "body," and "remains."

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchále nà jù shītǐ.
examples.english: The doctor examined the body.

examples.hanzi: 电视新闻说,警察找到了尸体。
examples.pinyin: Diànshì xīnwén shuō, jǐngchá zhǎodàole shītǐ.
examples.english: The TV news says the police found a body.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ dǎkāi chuānghu.
example.english: Please help me open the window.
example.fact: The 打 in 打开 has drifted far from its core meaning "to hit" — it functions here as a semantically bleached "light verb" that simply sets 开 ("open") into motion, the same bleached role 打 plays in 打电话 ("to make a phone call"), 打扫 ("to sweep, clean"), and 打算 ("to plan"), making 打 one of Mandarin's most overloaded verbs.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng dǎkāi nǐ de shū.
examples.english: Please open your book.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎkāile diànshì.
examples.english: He turned on the TV.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 检 first meant a wooden label or seal.
佥 (qiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn; also in 验 yàn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 险 xiǎn.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.

example.hanzi: 医生给我做了全面的检查。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi wǒ zuò le quánmiàn de jiǎnchá.
example.english: The doctor gave me a thorough examination.
example.fact: 检查 is the general, everyday word for looking something over — checking homework (检查作业) or a body (体检 is short for 身体检查) — while its more technical cousins 检验 and 检测 are reserved for laboratory testing or formal quality inspection, a specificity gradient among near-synonyms.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù yīyuàn zuò jiǎnchá.
examples.english: I'm going to the hospital for a checkup.

examples.hanzi: 老师在检查我们的作业。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài jiǎnchá wǒmen de zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher is checking our homework.
